decisions.reason: As a close extension of the firm's core door-hardware business, this classic handle line can be supported by existing design, engineering and sales knowledge, so management would be likely to retain it unless overlap within the range proves excessive.

This handle family is strongly related to the firm's established competences and broad assortment strategy, and the firm's in-house R&D raises its ability to refine rather than abandon such a product.

Although a single door-handle design can be more vulnerable to weak market reception than a full family, it is still very close to the firm's existing knowledge base and therefore likely to be improved and kept.
This product sits squarely within the firm's established architectural hardware expertise, so absorptive capacity and range-management experience make continuation more likely than withdrawal.

A door lever handle family fits the firm's core offer, benefits from existing certified systems and channel relationships, and in a growing industry a large German firm would usually keep such a related line.

The electronic access system is close to the firm's existing move into integrated digital building solutions, is presented as a flagship, and the firm's own R&D makes it especially likely to learn from early market feedback and continue investing in it.
